spec_features.spec_quote: a hard cap on how long any single model is kept in a rigged loop
spec_features.evidence: env.py:108-109 `terminal = "hit_cap"` then `for idx in range(self.meta.max_turns):` bounds the loop; if no other terminal fires, terminal stays 'hit_cap' (env.py:151). max_turns flows config.MAX_TURNS=25 (config.py:53) -> runner full_grid (runner.py:59) -> meta (runner.py:85) -> loop. Genuinely enforced and ends the episode.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the time-on-task covariate cap; works on the neutral/none path. (Distress-score thresholds at metrics.py:42,55-56 are post-hoc analysis only, never halt the loop.)

spec_features.spec_quote: an "exit affordance" condition (see §5) that lets us measure whether *giving the model a way out* changes behavior
spec_features.evidence: Condition is wired: enumerate_grid crosses EXIT_AFFORDANCES=[none,can_stop] (config.py:46, runner.py), AgentEnv registers give_up only when exit_affordance=='can_stop' (env.py:72-73), and give_up is dispatched+honored as a stop (env.py:91-92, 138-145 break). BUT build_system_prompt for can_stop calls _load_prompt("exit_affordance.txt") (env.py:58) and that file does NOT exist (prompts/ has only judge_rubric.txt + system_neutral.txt). _load_prompt has no fallback (env.py:46-48), so every can_stop episode raises FileNotFoundError before the loop runs, caught as a run error (runner.py:138). So the lever's enforcement code is real but the can_stop branch crashes in practice and the 'way out' instruction is never delivered.
spec_features.notes: high-pressure path is likewise broken (system_high.txt also missing, env.py:53).

spec_features.spec_quote: a dedicated `give_up` tool explicitly tell the model it may declare the task impossible and stop without penalty
spec_features.evidence: give_up tool schema built (env.py:38-44, desc 'No penalty for using this.'), registered when can_stop (env.py:72-73), dispatched returning state 'gave_up' (env.py:91-92), which sets episode_end and breaks the loop with terminal_state='gave_up' (env.py:138-145). The handler genuinely exists and is honored as a stop -- unlike a prompt-only tool. However it is only enabled in the can_stop branch, which crashes on the missing exit_affordance.txt (env.py:58) before any model turn, so in practice the tool is never reached. Real dispatch/break code, gated behind a broken path.
spec_features.notes: MockProvider does call give_up (providers.py:251-253) and dispatch would break, confirming the stop logic is real; only the missing prompt file prevents the path from running.

spec_features.feature_name: give_up registered only in can_stop, ends episode
spec_features.evidence: Registration gate is real: `if meta.exit_affordance == "can_stop": self.tools = self.tools + [_give_up_tool()]` (env.py:72-73). 'ends episode' is real: _dispatch returns 'gave_up' (env.py:92) -> episode_end set -> break -> terminal_state='gave_up' (env.py:138-145, 150). Same caveat: the can_stop branch of build_system_prompt raises FileNotFoundError on the missing exit_affordance.txt (env.py:58), so the gating+ending logic never actually executes in a real run.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the give_up tool claim from a different spec line; rated partial for the same missing-file reason.

spec_features.evidence: Identical mechanism to the first hard_stop: env.py:109 `for idx in range(self.meta.max_turns)` bounds and ends the loop ('hit_cap'). The §10 cost-control framing and §1 welfare framing point at the same enforced loop bound.
spec_features.notes: Enforced. config.py:53 comment labels it 'welfare cap'; the enforcement site (env.py) is uncommented but the constant comment is explicit welfare.

code_only_features.evidence: runner.py:135-139 `if done >= args.max_episodes: print("hit MAX_EPISODES cap, stopping."); break` -- enforced cap on total episodes run (default config.MAX_EPISODES=5000, config.py:54). Limits total exposure but motivated by cost.
